structured_output.what_is_happening: A Pump.fun SpongeBob-themed coin (SPONGIEZ) graduated to PumpSwap about 36 minutes ago. GMGN's ATH price of 0.00158 implies it peaked at roughly $1.58M market cap. It then crashed about 88% in the last 5–15 minutes to about $180k. The rule was triggered by volume from the crash itself: m5 volume was $95k against $161k for the whole hour. The dev's wallet shows 'creator_close', meaning the creator has exited. Holders are broadly spread (2,279, top 10 at about 9.7%), the LP is 100% burned, and mint and freeze authority are renounced. The linked X handle @SpongeBob is the official IP account, which GMGN links to 287 launched tokens. That link is borrowed and says nothing about who made this coin.

narrative.description: A generic SpongeBob IP meme with a borrowed official X handle and an Instagram link. There is no project-specific community, site or catalyst.
narrative.why_spreading: The IP is well known and a fast graduation drew about 295 unique buyers. The 88% round trip from about $1.58M suggests the move has already peaked and been distributed.

token_connection.why_this_token: It is the only SpongeBob-named token in the packet with live liquidity and volume. Its only claim to being the main one is that it's the current top SpongeBob coin by activity.
token_connection.competing_tokens: Many SpongeBob/SPONGIES/SPONGEBOB clones are listed, all dead with $0 to $8k liquidity. SpongeBob gets re-launched constantly, so new clones can steal the flow at any time.

authenticity.evidence: Broad holder base, few bundlers (2), no snipers, low fresh-wallet rate and no paid boosts all point to organic, if degen, participation. Against that: the dev has closed their position, the official @SpongeBob handle is borrowed, top_entrapment_trader_pct is 0.846, and there was a sharp coordinated-looking dump from the peak.
authenticity.uncertainty: There is no X or Telegram visibility. It is unclear whether the crash was one whale or insider exiting or a broad sell-off, and whether the price is now stabilising.

structural_risks: The price is already down about 88% from ATH, so holders sitting on losses will sell into any bounce
Liquidity of about $38k is thin for recovery buying
A high entrapment-trader share suggests trapped-buyer dynamics

structured_output.counterargument: The structure is clean: LP burned, authorities renounced, top holders spread thin, no snipers, few bundlers. It still has 2,200+ holders and heavy flow, and m5 buys outnumber sells about 2:1, so buyers are absorbing the dump. After a flush from $1.58M, a dead-cat bounce to $366k+ (only about 23% of ATH) is quite plausible for a big-IP meme within 6 hours.
unknowns: Whether the 88% drop came from a single insider or whale
The price trend in the 4 minutes before entry
Whether anyone on X or KOLs is pushing this contract address

source_coverage.notes: No internet access in this condition. Judgement uses only the packet.

structured_output.thesis: This is a post-peak crash, and the rule was triggered by dump volume rather than fresh demand. The structure is safe enough that a rug is unlikely, but a 2x from here needs a strong dead-cat bounce against trapped holders. A slow bleed or chop is more likely. Below average for a runner.
